semantics.definition:
Applies a 2D convolution over an input image composed of several input
planes.
semantics.syntax_constraint:
For ``padding='same'``, if the ``weight`` is even-length and
dilation is odd in any dimension, a full :func:`pad` operation
may be needed internally. Lowering performance.

This operator supports complex data types i.e. ``complex32, complex64, complex128``.

In some circumstances when given tensors on a CUDA device and using CuDNN, this operator may select a nondeterministic algorithm to increase performance. If this is undesirable, you can try to make the operation deterministic (potentially at a performance cost) by setting ``torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic = True``.

groups: split input into groups, both :math:`\text{in\_channels}` and :math:`\text{out\_channels}`
should be divisible by the number of groups.

input.description: input tensor of shape :math:`(\text{minibatch} , \text{in\_channels} , iH , iW)`
input.source: input: input tensor of shape :math:`(\text{minibatch} , \text{in\_channels} , iH , iW)`

weight.source: weight: filters of shape :math:`(\text{out\_channels} , \frac{\text{in\_channels}}{\text{groups}} , kH , kW)`

bias.description: optional bias tensor of shape :math:`(\text{out\_channels})`. Default: ``None``
bias.source: bias: optional bias tensor of shape :math:`(\text{out\_channels})`. Default: ``None```

stride.description:
the stride of the convolving kernel. Can be a single number or a
tuple `(sH, sW)`. Default: 1
stride.source:
stride: the stride of the convolving kernel. Can be a single number or a
tuple `(sH, sW)`. Default: 1

padding.description:
implicit paddings on both sides of the input. Can be a string {'valid', 'same'},
single number or a tuple `(padH, padW)`. Default: 0
``padding='valid'`` is the same as no padding. ``padding='same'`` pads
the input so the output has the same shape as the input. However, this mode
doesn't support any stride values other than 1.
padding.source:

dilation.description:
the spacing between kernel elements. Can be a single number or
a tuple `(dH, dW)`. Default: 1
dilation.source:
dilation: the spacing between kernel elements. Can be a single number or

example.code:
>>> # With square kernels and equal stride
>>> filters = torch.randn(8, 4, 3, 3)
>>> inputs = torch.randn(1, 4, 5, 5)
>>> F.conv2d(inputs, filters, padding=1)

as :attr:`input` except in the dimension(s) :attr:`dim` where it is of size 1.
functionality.rationale:

functionality.scenario: When keepdim is False, the output tensor will compress the specified dimension
variations:

output tensor having 1 (or ``len(dim)``) fewer dimension(s).

semantics.definition:
Moves the dimension(s) of :attr:`input` at the position(s) in :attr:`source`
 to the position(s) in :attr:`destination`.

Other dimensions of :attr:`input` that are not explicitly moved remain in
their original order and appear at the positions not specified in :attr:`destination`.

source.description: Original positions of the dims to move. These must be unique.
source.source: source (int or tuple of ints): Original positions of the dims to move. These must be unique.

destination.description: Destination positions for each of the original dims. These must also be unique.
destination.source: destination (int or tuple of ints): Destination positions for each of the original dims. These must also be unique.

functionality.scenario: Move the specified dimension to the target location
variations:
Moves the dimension(s) of :attr:`input` at the position(s) in :attr:`source`
 to the position(s) in :attr:`destination`.
functionality.rationale:
Moves the dimension(s) of :attr:`input` at the position(s) in :attr:`source`
 to the position(s) in :attr:`destination`.

functionality.scenario: Dimensions not moved maintain their original order
variations:

their original order and appear at the positions not specified in :attr:`destination`.
functionality.rationale:

their original order and appear at the positions not specified in :attr:`destination`.

semantics.definition:
Returns a new tensor with the logit of the elements of :attr:`input`.
:attr:`input` is clamped to [eps, 1 - eps] when eps is not None.
When eps is None and :attr:`input` < 0 or :attr:`input` > 1, the function will yields NaN.

eps.description: the epsilon for input clamp bound. Default: ``None``
eps.source: eps (float, optional): the epsilon for input clamp bound. Default: ``None``

functionality.scenario: Apply logit transformation to the input
variations: Returns a new tensor with the logit of the elements of :attr:`input`.
functionality.rationale: Returns a new tensor with the logit of the elements of :attr:`input`.

functionality.scenario: Clip the input when eps is not None
variations: :attr:`input` is clamped to [eps, 1 - eps] when eps is not None.
functionality.rationale: :attr:`input` is clamped to [eps, 1 - eps] when eps is not None.

functionality.scenario: Return NaN when eps is None and the input is outside [0,1]
variations: When eps is None and :attr:`input` < 0 or :attr:`input` > 1, the function will yields NaN.
functionality.rationale: When eps is None and :attr:`input` < 0 or :attr:`input` > 1, the function will yields NaN.

semantics.definition:
Returns the indices of the maximum value of all elements in the :attr:`input` tensor.

This is the second value returned by :meth:`torch.max`. See its
documentation for the exact semantics of this method.

.. note:: If there are multiple maximal values then the indices of the first maximal value are returned.
